text:
jordan-customer: Hey, seeing repeated disconnects and a 429 mid-stream during a single SSE session. Client got a partial output then the stream closed with a 429. Billing dashboard now shows ~3x token usage for that request. Request-id: abc123-redwood. Anyone seen this pattern?

jess-support: Ugh. Can you paste the raw SSE transcript you have and the curl/SDK call you used? Also which API key / org (no need to paste the secret) and the timestamp for the call?

jordan-customer: Here's the trace I captured from the client (trimmed):

```
: open
event: response
data: {"id":"res_abc","object":"text_stream","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hello, here is a very long answer..."}}]}

event: response
data: {"id":"res_abc","object":"text_stream","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...continuing"}}]}

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 2
content-type: application/json

{"error":{"message":"quota exceeded","type":"rate_limit"},"request_id":"abc123-redwood"}
```

And the client automatically retried the stream once (it reconnects on transient network by default). The curl I used (simplified):

```
curl -N https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/stream \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"longform-2","stream":true,"max_tokens":16000,"prompt":"<huge_prompt>"}'
```

The dashboard shows 12k tokens billed for that request whereas the model response was only ~4k tokens.

mike-sre: Thanks — that snapshot is super helpful. Two quick possibilities: (1) server hit per-token quota mid-generation and returned 429, then client retried which triggered the model to re-generate the same tokens and we double-counted on billing; or (2) there's an auth/token rotation race that caused the request to be validated twice on different backends.

Can you confirm whether your client retried automatically after the 429 or if it resumed from the last event? Many clients simply reopen the SSE and expect the server to resume at a cursor, but our streaming API doesn't support automatic cursor resumption — a new connection starts a new generation.

jordan-customer: The client did a reconnect/retry exactly once after the 429. It did not attempt to resume. So it sounds like case (1).

arjun-runtime: Looping in runtime. Hi — from the runtime perspective, we increment token counters whenever a flush to the client is acknowledged by the transport layer. If a client reconnects and the generator restarts, we should not double-charge for the already-delivered tokens unless the generator replays tokens and we count them again. We recently shipped a small change that makes per-chunk ack semantics more aggressive; if the client reconnects during an in-flight flush we might be counting the chunk twice.

support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-489 (streaming 429 -> duplicate token billing). Assigned: eng-runtime.

mike-sre: For triage please provide: full request headers (redact secrets), full server-side log slice for request_id=abc123-redwood, and the client retry behavior (exact timing of reconnect). If you can reproduce, please run with `STREAM_DEBUG=true` in the SDK or pass `x-debug-mode: stream-ack` header and grab logs.

jordan-customer: I attached the server response headers I captured and timestamps: initial stream start 2026-03-10T14:02:36Z, 429 at 2026-03-10T14:02:58Z, client reconnect at 2026-03-10T14:03:01Z. Server headers on first connection included: `X-Quota-Remaining: 0` which is weird because our org quota shouldn't have been exhausted.

arjun-runtime: That header is useful — it suggests quota enforcement fired at the backend. Two actions from runtime side: (A) check whether chunk-level ack increments are idempotent across reconnections; (B) audit the billing pipeline to see whether reconnections are being recorded as separate billable requests.

jess-support: For immediate mitigation: you can (1) set your client to not auto-retry on 429 for streaming sessions, or (2) reduce `max_tokens` so the request is less likely to cross quota thresholds, or (3) switch to a non-streaming generation for this particular long prompt to avoid ack semantics. Any of those would avoid duplicate charges while we fix server-side.

mike-sre: Also checking whether rate limiter is per-session vs per-auth-token. If the limiter is per-token and we had quick reconnects, the second connection might see a new per-connection allowance. That mismatch could lead to both connections being allowed to produce tokens which were each billed.

arjun-runtime: I found a relevant snippet in the runtime change log: we introduced optimistic ack counting to improve tail latency. It was supposed to be guarded by `--ack-idempotent=true` but that flag wasn't respected in the streaming path. So in a reconnect scenario the same chunk can be counted twice. Working on a hotfix to revert the optimistic ack until we implement idempotency tokens.

support-bot: Patch branch created: git/infra/streaming-ack-revert (PR #1221). Test CI triggered.

jordan-customer: Appreciate the fast turnaround. Will the hotfix also reconcile billing so that we don't bill the duplicate tokens? The invoice already showed the spike.

mike-sre: Short answer: we will refund obvious duplicate charges once the bug is confirmed and we can correlate double-billing by request_id and timing. Please file a billing ticket referencing INC-2026-489 and include the invoice id. We'll queue reconciliation.

arjun-runtime: Timeline: hotfix patch in next 2–4 hours, staged to canary, full rollout if canary metrics look good. When rolling back optimistic ack we'll also add a server-side guard to de-duplicate on reconnects by checking `x-client-session` header if present — if not present we'll require clients to send `client_session_id` for long streaming jobs. We'll add an SDK update to surface `client_session_id` automatically.

jordan-customer: Can you confirm whether any data leakage is possible when a reconnect occurs? We care about partial outputs and PII.

arjun-runtime: No evidence of cross-customer leakage. Reconnects start a fresh generation scoped to the same auth key; they don't replay other customers' tokens. We'll include an automated check in the canary to validate that.

jess-support: Action items for customer: 1) Please set client to not auto-retry on 429 for streaming until we finish the patch. 2) Share invoice id and request_id (abc123-redwood) in the billing ticket. 3) If you can reproduce, run with `STREAM_DEBUG=true` and upload full logs.

jordan-customer: Done — billing ticket filed (BT-55812) with invoice and request id. Also reproduced locally with `curl -N` by forcing a `X-Force-Quota-Exhaust: true` header (test header we use). I can run more traces if you want.

mike-sre: Great. We'll track INC-2026-489 and BT-55812 together. I'll post updates in this thread. Thanks for the quick reproduction — that really speeds up reconciliation. :thumbsup:

support-bot: INC-2026-489 status updated: in_progress -> investigating. PR #1221 created.

arjun-runtime: Follow-up note for eng: check billing pipeline consumer `billing-stream-consumer` to ensure it deduplicates by `(request_id, session_epoch)` and add a lookback query to find likely double-charges between 2026-03-10T13:50Z and 2026-03-10T15:00Z.

mike-sre: I'll also look at rate limiter config — maybe tighten `burst_allowance` for streaming connections to avoid mid-stream 429s when budget is low.

jordan-customer: Thanks all. I'll keep client retries off and will follow up if I see more. Appreciate the help and the quick incident response.

jess-support: Closing loop when refund is processed. Will update thread. :eyes:
